A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same origin-attribution study, with readable text, equations, six figures, eight tables, and both supplementary sections. No material gaps prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original membership-inference, model-attribution and origin-attribution experiments, plus feature ablations and supplementary CIFAR-10 classification results in Tables 7–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons in Tables 4–6 and experiments in Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same timestep-wise loss and gradient-norm features, followed by the linear classifier in Equation 9. The appendix PIA variant is unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies the existing trajectory construction without altering its procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain CIFAR-10, CIFAR-10.1, CelebA-HQ 256, FFHQ-256, and generated-image scenarios involving DDIM, DDGAN and WaveDiff. MIA, MA, OA and supplementary CIFAR-10 classification coverage are unchanged. Stable Diffusion appears only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains Matsumoto et al., Kong's PIA, Pang's GSA2 and the model-blind baseline; Tables 5–6 retain their model-blind comparisons. Pang's citation year changes from 2023 to 2024, but the evaluated comparator is unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported training and evaluation sample selection, Table 1 hyperparameters, feature normalization, timestep selections and evaluation metrics are unchanged. The supplementary classifier still uses 1,000 class-balanced training samples and a separate similarly selected evaluation set.

E4.justification: Both retain the timestep-sampling analysis, feature visualizations, learned-weight analysis, OA filtering case study, feature ablations and supplementary class-prediction experiment. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The same point-estimate tables and plotted summaries are retained. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 retain identical result entries, and Figures 2–6 retain their empirical content. For example, Table 4's full-feature CIFAR-10 MIA AUC remains 83.3, while Table 8's accuracies remain 26.5, 31.4 and 31.6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the mathematical feature definitions are retained. The new trajectory footnote clarifies the unchanged construction's relationship to DDPMs; it introduces no new definition, derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the contributions retain the same scope: surrogate-free trajectory-based attacks, benefits from gradient features, and MIA, MA and OA capabilities. The revised contribution wording does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly qualifies the trajectory as non-native to DDPMs. The runtime limitation loses its worst-case qualifier. Section 5.4 replaces feature-selection and nonuniform-timestep proposals with Stable Diffusion extension and the distribution-shift challenges of diverse training data.

D1.justification: The operational implementation information remains the same: Algorithm 1, classifier hyperparameters, optimization and normalization details, and repository access footnotes. No new implementation setting or resource availability is disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 newly attributes the forward trajectory construction to Huberman-Spiegelglas et al. (2024), already cited in v1 for inversion. This refines the method's relationship to prior work; reference membership remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds numbered sections and subsections, Appendix A–B labels, precise cross-references, and copyediting throughout. Several passages are rephrased, but section order and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn from a single-image pipeline with database icons into multiple image examples and illustrated class regions. Other changes comprise caption edits and limited text reflow; empirical figures and table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity by explicitly identifying the non-native trajectory construction in Section 3.3 and providing precise numbered section and appendix references. The revised schematic and prose aid explanation, while the experimental evidence and substantive limitations remain essentially unchanged.
